To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
renal epithelial cells (RECs) are exposed to oxalate (Ox) and calcium oxalates (CaOx) crystals in vivo.
renal epithelial cells are susceptible to injury from oxalate and CaOx crystals.
renal epithelial cells exposed to oxalate crystals and calcium oxalates develop a pro-inflammatory response, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of kidney stones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which calcium oxalate monohydrate crystals (COM) damage renal epithelial cells.
the molecular mechanisms of calcium oxalate (CaOx) nephrolithiasis.
understanding the pathogenesis of calcium oxalate urolithiasis, and with developing methods for the prevention and treatment of this condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important risk factor for the development of nephrolithiasis is a high urinary oxalate excretion.
the presence of a stone in the urinary tract is not a benign event.
calcium oxalate stone disease is the result of an imbalance of oxalate excretion and calcium absorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the renal epithelial cells are sensitive to oxalate exposure and that calcium oxalate crystallization is a key event in renal epithelial cell damage.

the presence of crystals in renal epithelial cell cultures leads to the activation of intracellular signaling pathways, resulting in changes in gene and protein expression that are associated with the development of nephrolithiasis.

the results of this study indicate that the renal epithelial cell line MDCK is sensitive to the toxic effects of oxalate and CaOx crystals, and that the toxic effects of CaOx crystals are mediated, at least in part, via the generation of reactive oxygen species.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of crystals can lead to the activation of the inflammasomes, a family of intracellular sensors that detect the presence of pathogens and other danger signals, and trigger a pro-inflammatory response.
we have shown a novel mechanism by which the kidney is damaged by oxalate.
the calcium oxalate crystal-induced cell injury and cell death are mediated by calcium oxalate and not by oxalate.
